title: Planning clients observe external gateway writers without Refresh
description: Draft7 browser proof on an isolated gateway/UI. Independent RPC writers and raw roadmap file create/edit/atomic replacement/delete update mounted canonical panels without Refresh. A real read error preserves an unsaved draft; new offline documents restore four planning collections from SQLite with original observation times, visible ages and disabled actual actions, then recover. Configure an isolated home/farm/profile/ports, disabled orchestration, a disposable offline-planning-* project and fresh artifacts. Mobile/desktop and authority-revocation proofs remain separate. Configuration file and second-client writes update mounted policy. Real project collections below/above2MiB are checked against SQLite and new offline documents; client project replies exclude declared webhook secrets.

proofTargets.claim: Independent gateway writers update canonical planning observations and their rendered backlog, roadmap, graph and queue content without Refresh.
A backlog status filter excludes its candidate while retaining the canonical collection and selected identity.
An external roadmap file creation reaches the open canonical collection and rendered row without Refresh.
An external roadmap file edit reaches the same mounted canonical collection and rendered row without Refresh.
An atomic roadmap file replacement reaches the same mounted canonical collection and rendered row without Refresh.
An external roadmap file deletion removes the canonical and rendered row without Refresh.
A real roadmap read failure and disconnect retain the unsaved draft, selection and base hash with actions disabled.
Four planning collections restore exact saved observation times, visible age and disabled actions offline, then recover.
External project edits, atomic replacement and second-client policy writes update mounted configuration without Refresh; project replies omit webhook secrets.
A real project collection persists below2MiB with exact cold rows/age/disabled writes; an oversized collection evicts and is absent offline, then recovers.
